keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Ammon (its Neo-Assyrian shape of -700 contains the same land as imperial territory). The page gives no area; it describes the country as lying between the Arnon and Jabbok valleys. The gazetteer's Ammon region (Amman, Balqa and Zarqa governorates, about 6,000 km2) is the researcher's reading. Heshbon is not placed by this page; Jabesh-Gilead 'lay outside the territory he laid claim to'.

ledger.note: c. 1050 BCE: the Kingdom of Ammon flourishes at Rabbath Ammon. The page's earliest dated entry is 'Kingdom of Ammon flourishes: 11th century BC' and it gives no founding date or founder; King Nahash 'c. 1010 - 990 BC' lay siege to Jabesh-Gilead. A century is not a year; mid-century is a convention.

region.text: Ammon 'between the torrent valleys of Arnon and Jabbok', with its chief city Rabbah or Rabbat Ammon, the site of modern Amman

ledger.note: 734 BC: Ammon pays tribute to Assyria. 'In 734 BC the Ammonite king Sanipu was a vassal of Tiglath-Pileser III of Assyria'; the Tiglath-Pileser III page lists 'Moab and Ammon' among those who 'began paying tribute' in the campaign of 734. Pudu-ilu 'held the same position under Sennacherib (r. 705-681) and Esarhaddon (r. 681-669)' and Amminadab I (fl. 650 BC) was among the tributaries.

ledger.note: c. 609 BCE (bridged): Assyria's overlordship ends. No page opened dates when Ammon stopped paying Assyria; the year mirrors the neo-assyrian-empire dossier's close of the 734 tributaries.

region.text: Ammon 'between the torrent valleys of Arnon and Jabbok', with its chief city Rabbah or Rabbat Ammon, the site of modern Amman

ledger.note: c. 609 BCE (bridged): Ammon is under Babylon. 'Ammon flourished during the period of the Neo-Babylonian Empire (626 to 539 BC)'; the Nebuchadnezzar page has the kings of Ammon, Edom, Moab, Sidon and Tyre meeting at Jerusalem in 594 BC to discuss throwing off Babylonian control, and 'In 587 BC, Ammon, Edom and Moab likewise rebelled'. The start of Babylonian overlordship is undated. [Reviewer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: year moved from -609 to -605: the Nebuchadnezzar II page says the victory at Carchemish in 605 BC 'resulted in all of Syria and Israel coming under the control of the Neo-Babylonian Empire' and puts no Babylonian overlordship in the Levant before 605; 609 is the fall of Harran, not Babylon's arrival.]

ledger.note: 580s BC: Ammon is annexed by Babylon. 'Ammon became a Babylonian province, shortly after being devastated by Nebuchadnezzar II in the 580s BC'; the Ammonite king Baalis, linked to the assassination of Gedaliah, is undated on the page.

region.text: Ammon 'between the torrent valleys of Arnon and Jabbok', with its chief city Rabbah or Rabbat Ammon, the site of modern Amman

ledger.note: 580s BC: the Kingdom of Ammon ends as a province of Babylon. The page gives no end for the kingdom; after this the Ammonites 'enjoyed continuity from the Neo-Babylonian to the Persian period' and Rabbath Amman was 'seized by Ptolemy II' around 255 BC.

wars.name: Nahash's siege of Jabesh-Gilead
wars.outcome: 'King Nahash of Ammon (c. 1010 - 990 BC) lay siege to Jabesh-Gilead'; the page gives no outcome and says the town 'lay outside the territory he laid claim to'.
wars.note: The page dates Nahash's reign, not the siege. The Israel dossier (me-04-a) carries Ammon as David's client c. 1000-930 from the united-monarchy page; the Ammon page says only that 'the Ammonites humiliated David's messengers' (undated).

wars.name: Battle of Qarqar
wars.outcome: Assyrian claim of victory; the coalition's thrones survived. Ba'asa son of Ruhubi of Ammon sent about 100 soldiers (Qarqar page).
wars.note: The Ammon page names 'Baasha ben Ruhubi' at Qarqar in 853 BC (another passage 854).

notes: Cliopatria has no Ammon; Cliopatria's Neo-Assyrian (-700), Neo-Babylonian and Achaemenid shapes contain the same land as direct imperial territory, so the vassal tint depends on this dossier. Early life is thin: the page gives only 'the 11th century BC' and Nahash's reign (c. 1010-990). The 1050 start is a century's middle; David's overlordship (kingdom-of-israel dossier, vassal -1000 to -930) is not on the Ammon page. The end (580s BC) is the page's 'Babylonian province' sentence; the 609 hand-over from Assyria to Babylon is bridged (mirrors neo-assyrian-empire's -609). Moab's page, by contrast, is silent on a Babylonian annexation and ends c. 400 BCE, so the two neighbours disagree on the pages opened. Heshbon (border town between Moab and Ammon) and the Jabbok line are unplaced. Page budget: four pages (two shared with the Moab dossier).
